sentences.text: Pseudocrypturus was an extinct bird belonging to the paleognathous group, which includes modern ostriches.
Its scientific name translates to 'false tinamou', distinguishing it from other ancient relatives.
The specific name cercanaxius highlights the bird's rudimentary pygostyle, a small tail structure found in some modern birds.
The holotype fossil, which defines the species, is currently kept at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History.
Remains were discovered in the Fossil Butte Member of the Green River Formation in Wyoming.
Taxonomically, Pseudocrypturus is placed within the family Lithornithidae.
This animal lived during the Early Eocene epoch, specifically between 56 and 51.1 million years ago.
